text:
Chandra: heads up — p95 east-west latency spike across rack-7 during the 18:00 batching window, started ~18:02 and lasted ~2.5m. GPUs saw tail latency climb ~270ms, some pods hit SLOs. ops-bot alerted.
Maya: ack. are we seeing packet loss counters or MTU mismatches? any recent config or kernel rollouts to that rack?
AJ: no kernel rollouts in rack-7. I see small RX drops on eth3 on node gpu-7-12 around the time. ethtool shows rx_errors bumped.
Luca: grabbing ifconfig + ethtool dumps now. can someone pull rdma counters? `ibstat` and `ibv_devinfo`?
ops-bot: ALERT: cluster-alerts — east-west-p95 > 200ms (rack-7). Incident-ID: INC-20240315-72
Chandra: copy. AJ, paste ethtool output when you have it. Maya, can you check the qdisc and if there were any tc changes?
AJ: ethtool -S eth3 snippet: "rx_no_buffer_count: 0", "rx_errors: 142", "tx_errors: 0", "rx_missed_errors: 9". Also saw some fragmented frames counters increase in kernel logs.
Maya: `tc -s qdisc show dev eth3` shows pfifo_fast default, no policing. no recent tc jobs in audit logs.
Luca: RDMA side: `ibv_devinfo -v` looks fine. `ibportstat` shows only occasional retransmits, but at the same times p95 spikes we see a burst of 'dropped frames due to too small MTU' on kernel dmesg on gpu-7-12.
Chandra: too-small MTU? did anything touch MTU on ToR or host? Could be path MTU blackhole or a middlebox. 
AJ: ToR config unchanged. But I see an automated daemon re-applied network configs on that host at 17:58 (kube node reconfigure job). It set host MTU to 1500 while ToR expects 9000 for RDMA.
Maya: that would explain fragmentation and retransmits. if host MTU=1500 and switch expects jumbo, packets get fragmented and RDMA/DPDK flows degrade. 
Luca: confirming: `ip link show` on gpu-7-12: mtu 1500. Neighbor nodes still 9000. So asymmetric MTU in the path.
Chandra: roll back MTU to 9000 on gpu-7-12 and restart rdma services. Who can run the change? Ops runbook: `sudo ip link set dev eth3 mtu 9000 && systemctl restart rdma`.
AJ: running now on gpu-7-12.
ops-bot: DEPLOY-BOT: network-change job queued by AJ (job-9821).
AJ: done. post-change quick checks: `ip link show` mtu 9000, `dmesg` clear of fragmentation messages, rdma counters back to baseline. 
Maya: observing latency graph: p95 back down to baseline within ~30s of change. no errors in 18:06–18:10 window.
Chandra: root cause: automated config reapply on node reverted MTU to default 1500. Action items: (1) prevent node-local daemon from overwriting MTU (add whitelist), (2) add MTU drift monitor + alert, (3) run a sweep to detect other nodes with wrong MTU. 
Luca: I'll file infra ticket and add a preflight check to the node-config job. Ticket INFRA-2345.
AJ: one more ask — add a quick runbook snippet for on-call: `if p95 east-west spike && rdma errors -> check ip link mtu mismatch`.
Chandra: agreed. Thanks team. Closing thread once tickets are created.
Luca: INFRA-2345 created, assigned to netops. I'll follow up with postmortem note.
Maya: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: INC-20240315-72 -> status: resolved (18:07)
